value_stream.name: Store Remodel, Renovation & Lifecycle Refurbishment Program

fields.Participants: Marketing (links to VS-14), Store Manager (links to VS-07), Merchandising (links to VS-01), Loyalty (links to VS-13), Regional Manager (links to VS-07)

workflows.name: Remodel Soft Launch / Grand Re-opening & Marketing

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "loyalty-member and trade-account outreach" lists (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-verify of "ecommerce inventory/price sync" against the new store state (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-capture of "footfall/sales/feedback" into the re-opening scorecard (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-558 (ensure controlled execution — Re-merchandising, Re-opening & Remodel Performance Analytics (PA-109.3).)
- operational: targeted trade-area campaign; operational: ecommerce sync check (links to VS-10)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Weak-launch risk**: Poor marketing caps the remodel's sales lift; mitigated by targeted trade-area campaign
- **Channel-inconsistency risk**: Online inventory/price out of sync with the new store; mitigated by ecommerce sync check (links to VS-10)
System Touchpoints: - Marketing (links to VS-14); loyalty (links to VS-13); POS (links to VS-08); ecommerce (links to VS-10); promotions (links to VS-58); PR/community (links to VS-14.3/VS-104)

steps.activity: Marketing/Store Manager plan the re-opening: soft-launch (staff/VIP/trade links to VS-43) followed by grand re-opening event, local marketing (links to VS-14.1), loyalty-member and trade-account outreach (links to VS-13/VS-43), re-opening promotions (links to VS-58/VS-14), and PR/community (links to VS-14.3/VS-104)

Marketing/Merchandising execute re-opening offers, trade-area catchment marketing, and signage/POS materials (links to VS-14.1/W3485); ensure the loyalty engine (links to VS-13), POS (links to VS-08), and ecommerce inventory/price sync (links to VS-10) reflect the new store state

Store Manager/Marketing run the re-opening event, capture footfall/sales/feedback (links to VS-13/VS-44), and transition to steady-state operations (links to VS-07); report re-opening results to the program review (W3491/W3496)

fields.Participants: Store Manager (links to VS-07), L&D (links to VS-19.4), IT (links to VS-27), Merchandising (links to VS-01), Change/PMO (links to VS-112)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "L&D/Store Manager plan the remodel training" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-validate of "checkout readiness before re-opening" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-post of "Store Manager/Change Mgmt manage the change" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-558 (ensure controlled execution — Re-merchandising, Re-opening & Remodel Performance Analytics (PA-109.3).)
- operational: reinforcement and on-floor coaching; operational: pre-opening verification
Pain Points / Risks: - **Adoption risk**: Staff revert to old ways; mitigated by reinforcement and on-floor coaching
- **Checkout-readiness risk**: Staff not fluent on new POS at re-opening; mitigated by pre-opening verification
System Touchpoints: - L&D (links to VS-19.4); IT/POS (links to VS-08/VS-27); HR/EX (links to VS-103.2); merchandising (links to VS-01); PMO (links to VS-112)

steps.activity: L&D/Store Manager plan the remodel training: new POS/technology (links to VS-08/W3486), new assortment/categories and product knowledge (links to VS-01/W3478), new layout/wayfinding, new service offers, and brand/customer-experience standards (links to VS-13); schedule pre-opening training

L&D/Merchandising/IT deliver training to store staff (and any new hires links to VS-19.1): classroom, on-the-job, vendor training (links to W1099), and quick-reference guides; verify competence/checkout readiness before re-opening

Store Manager/Change Mgmt manage the change: communication, address staff concerns, reinforce new ways-of-working in the first weeks post re-opening (links to VS-103.2 EX), and capture adoption issues; feed training gaps to L&D (links to VS-19.4)

fields.Participants: FP&A (links to VS-17.4/VS-33.2), VP Store Operations, Merchandising (links to VS-01/VS-101), BI (links to VS-28.1), Regional Manager (links to VS-07)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-track of "track post-remodel performance" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-reconcile of "reconcile actual lift to the business case" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "VP Store Operations/FP&A report remodel performance to the program" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-558 (ensure controlled execution — Re-merchandising, Re-opening & Remodel Performance Analytics (PA-109.3).)
- operational: control-store comparison; operational: root-cause and corrective action
Pain Points / Risks: - **Lift-attribution risk**: Macro/seasonality mistaken for remodel lift; mitigated by control-store comparison
- **Benefit-shortfall risk**: Lift below business case; mitigated by root-cause and corrective action
System Touchpoints: - BI/FP&A (links to VS-28.1/VS-17.4/VS-33.2); merchandising (links to VS-01/VS-101); inventory (links to VS-05); capex/benefits (links to VS-40/W3561)

steps.activity: FP&A/BI track post-remodel performance: comp-sales lift vs pre-remodel baseline and vs non-remodeled control stores, traffic, ATV/basket, category mix (links to VS-01), gross margin (links to VS-101), inventory turn (links to VS-05), and conversion; normalize for seasonality and external factors

FP&A/Merchandising reconcile actual lift to the business case (W3476): payback/IRR tracking, lost-sales recovery, and category-level contribution; identify laggards and root cause (assortment, pricing, marketing, macro)

VP Store Operations/FP&A report remodel performance to the program review (W3496) and executives (links to VS-33.2), re-baseline laggards, and feed insights to future remodel concepts (W3475) and the roadmap (W3473/W3495)

fields.Participants: CX (links to VS-13), Consumer Insights (links to VS-44), Store Manager (links to VS-07), Marketing (links to VS-14), BI (links to VS-28.1)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "reviews, and trade-account feedback" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-validate of "assess the experience" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "report CX impact vs the business case" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-558 (ensure controlled execution — Re-merchandising, Re-opening & Remodel Performance Analytics (PA-109.3).)
- operational: mystery shopping and VOC; operational: sampling and mixed channels
Pain Points / Risks: - **Friction-blindspot risk**: Post-remodel friction unnoticed; mitigated by mystery shopping and VOC
- **Over-survey risk**: Feedback fatigue; mitigated by sampling and mixed channels
System Touchpoints: - CX/VOC (links to VS-13/VS-44.1); mystery shopping (links to VS-55.2); BI (links to VS-28.1); POS speed (links to VS-08)

steps.activity: CX/Insights capture post-remodel customer feedback: NPS/CSAT (links to VS-13/VS-44.1), store-visit surveys, mystery shopping (links to VS-55.2/VS-44), social/reviews, and trade-account feedback (links to VS-43); compare to pre-remodel baseline and peer stores

CX/Store Manager assess the experience: layout/wayfinding ease, department findability, checkout speed (links to VS-08), service quality, ambiance/lighting, and cleanliness; identify strengths and friction points

CX/Insights feed findings to the store (corrective) and to the program review (W3496/format innovation W3495): replicate successful design choices, fix recurring friction in the next concept, and report CX impact vs the business case (W3476)

fields.Participants: Project Manager (links to VS-112), Finance/FP&A (links to VS-40/VS-17.4), Real Estate, Store Manager (links to VS-07), Procurement (links to VS-03/VS-34)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-record of "Project Manager conduct the post-implementation review" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "Finance/PMO report PIR outcomes to the program review" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: closure discipline; operational: knowledge management (W3494)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unclosed-project risk**: Open POs/commitments distort the portfolio; mitigated by closure discipline
- **Lesson-loss risk**: PIR lessons not captured/reused; mitigated by knowledge management (W3494)
System Touchpoints: - Capex/closure (links to VS-40/W1825/W1828); PMO/PMIS (links to VS-112); FP&A (links to VS-17.4); audit (links to VS-21); vendor scorecard (links to VS-67)

steps.activity: Finance/Project Manager close the project financially: final cost vs budget (links to VS-40/W1825), commitment/PO closure, retention release (W3482), CIP-to-asset turnover (links to VS-40/W1828/W3560), and capex-portfolio reconciliation (links to VS-112/W3564)

Project Manager conduct the post-implementation review (PIR): scope delivered vs planned, schedule variance, cost variance and drivers (change orders W3556, scope, market), quality/snag closure (W3488), HSE record (links to VS-24), and contractor performance (links to VS-67)
Finance/PMO report PIR outcomes to the program review (W3496) and audit (links to VS-21), feed lessons to W3494, and update the capex-portfolio and PMO analytics (links to VS-112/W3563)

fields.Participants: PMO (links to VS-112), Real Estate, Store Design, Merchandising (links to VS-01), Project Managers, Facilities (links to VS-20.3)

workflows.name: Remodel Lessons Learned & Store-Lifecycle Knowledge Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-schedule of "schedule/quality/HSE learnings, and store/customer feedback" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-issue of "issues, high/low-performing concepts" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "track whether prior lessons were applied and effective" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-558 (ensure controlled execution — Re-merchandising, Re-opening & Remodel Performance Analytics (PA-109.3).)
- operational: tracking application and governance (W3496); operational: centralized knowledge base
Pain Points / Risks: - **Lesson-non-reuse risk**: Lessons captured but not applied; mitigated by tracking application and governance (W3496)
- **Knowledge-silo risk**: Lessons stuck with individual PMs; mitigated by centralized knowledge base
System Touchpoints: - PMO/PMIS (links to VS-112); knowledge base (links to VS-30.3/VS-88); design/space (links to VS-55); vendor (links to VS-03/VS-67); performance (links to VS-28.1)

steps.activity: PMO/Project Managers capture lessons per project (from PIR W3493): what worked, what didn't, design/procurement/construction/phasing/vendor insights, cost/schedule/quality/HSE learnings, and store/customer feedback (W3492); structure for reuse

PMO/Real Estate synthesize portfolio lessons quarterly: recurring design issues, high/low-performing concepts (links to W3491), best-performing vendors/fixtures, common permit/construction friction (links to W3479/W3483), and cost benchmarks; publish to the knowledge base (links to VS-30.3/VS-88)
PMO feed lessons into the next concept cycle (W3475), design standards (W3477), vendor frameworks (W3482), and the program governance (W3496); track whether prior lessons were applied and effective

fields.Participants: VP Store Operations, Real Estate, Facilities (links to VS-20.3), Finance (links to VS-40/VS-17.4), Merchandising (links to VS-01)
fields.Trigger: Annual planning (links to VS-33.1); lifecycle analytics (W3491)

workflows.name: Store Refurbishment Cadence & Lifecycle Refresh Planning

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-forecast of "forecast the multi-year refresh demand" (replaces manual Step 1).
Controls: - CTL-558 (ensure controlled execution — Re-merchandising, Re-opening & Remodel Performance Analytics (PA-109.3).)
- operational: cadence discipline and lifecycle modeling; operational: ROI-based mix optimization
Pain Points / Risks: - **Deferral-accumulation risk**: Pushing refreshes forward balloons future capex; mitigated by cadence discipline and lifecycle modeling
- **Mix-misoptimization risk**: Too many light refreshes vs full remodels under-delivers; mitigated by ROI-based mix optimization
System Touchpoints: - Store-lifecycle/asset (links to VS-35/VS-97); facility (links to VS-20.3); capex (links to VS-40/VS-112); strategy/performance (links to VS-33/VS-28.1); store ops (links to VS-07)

steps.activity: Real Estate/Facilities maintain the store-lifecycle and refurbishment-cadence model: per-store age, last-remodel date, fixture/MEP condition, comp trajectory (links to W3474), and the tiered refresh plan (full remodel / refresh / re-fixture / repaint-and-repair); forecast the multi-year refresh demand

VP Store Operations/Finance balance the refresh cadence against the capital plan (links to VS-40/VS-33.1) and new-store growth (links to VS-37): optimize the mix of full remodels vs light refreshes vs re-fixtures to maximize portfolio ROI under the capex constraint

VP Store Operations/Real Estate publish the multi-year refresh roadmap and integrate to the store-lifecycle strategy (W3473), new-store (links to VS-37) and closure (links to VS-59) plans, and the capex portfolio (links to VS-40/VS-112); refresh annually with performance data (W3491)

fields.Participants: VP Store Operations, COO, CFO, CMO, Real Estate, Merchandising (links to VS-01), Strategy (links to VS-33), PMO (links to VS-112)
fields.Trigger: Annual strategy review; board/exec cycle (links to VS-33/VS-36)

workflows.name: Store Format Innovation & Remodel Program Governance

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-capture of "drive store-format innovation" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "conduct the quarterly remodel-program review" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System rule-based auto-approval of "approve policy/standard updates" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: piloting and benchmarking; operational: quarterly governance and board oversight
Pain Points / Risks: - **Innovation-stagnation risk**: Format fails to evolve with the market; mitigated by piloting and benchmarking
- **Program-drift risk**: Remodels drift from strategy/ROI targets; mitigated by quarterly governance and board oversight
System Touchpoints: - Strategy/performance (links to VS-33); PMO (links to VS-112); capex (links to VS-40); merchandising (links to VS-01); board reporting (links to VS-36); digital/solar (links to VS-75/VS-70/VS-108)

steps.activity: VP Store Operations/Merchandising drive store-format innovation: pilot new concepts/formats (e.g., appliance-gallery format, project-design center links to VS-66, renewable/solar bay links to VS-70/VS-108, digital-first store links to VS-75), test in a remodel, and scale successful concepts into the standard; benchmark competitors and global retail (links to VS-33.3)
steps.r: VP Store Operations / Merchandising / Store Design

steps.activity: VP Store Operations/PMO conduct the quarterly remodel-program review: portfolio progress (links to VS-112), performance vs business case (W3491/W3561), capex variance (W3493), lessons (W3494), refresh cadence (W3495), and vendor/design performance (links to VS-67); decide adjustments and resource allocation

COO/CFO report the remodel program (performance, capex, format innovation, store-lifecycle health) to the executive committee (links to VS-33.2) and Board (links to VS-36); ensure alignment with corporate strategy, capital, and store-growth plans and approve policy/standard updates
